Issues.Title: fix(wpf): use UTF-8 for native compilation
Issues.Body:
Append /source-charset:utf-8 /execution-charset:utf-8 to inherited compiler options in the shared Wpf.Cpp.props. Also replace the em dash with an ASCII `-`.

Fixes #11996

## Description

On Windows code page 936, MSVC interprets UTF-8 source files without a BOM using the host code page. The em dashes in DirectWriteForwarder's TtfDelta comments trigger C4819/C2220 and stop the WPF build.

Append `/source-charset:utf-8 /execution-charset:utf-8` to inherited compiler options in the shared `Wpf.Cpp.props`. Source-only UTF-8 settings expose C4566 for `©` in generated C++ assembly attributes on this machine; explicitly selecting the execution charset preserves the copyright text.

Replace three comment em dashes with ASCII hyphens. The three-file patch changes the common compiler configuration and comments.

## Customer Impact

Contributors using affected Windows code pages cannot build WPF from source. An explicit encoding makes this build behavior independent of the host code page. End-user application impact has not been demonstrated.

## Regression

Reproduces at WPF commit `e89a851c5792c8777a7115cc7a797fd0c045fdd4`. The first affected release or commit has not been established.

## Testing

- WPF Windows x64 Release restore/build/pack/publish through the VMR passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors; dependencies were reused, and the native projects actually recompiled.
- All 29 actual compiler command logs include both charset options.
- CLR metadata in `DirectWriteForwarder.dll` and `System.Printing.dll` preserves `© Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.`.
- Inspected 1,382 WPF-owned source/header inputs, including generated files. The only non-ASCII or Unicode-escape literal candidates were the two copyright attributes.
- Exported with `darc vmr diff` and applied to an independent WPF checkout at the synchronized revision. The resulting sources match the validated sources; patch application and whitespace checks passed.

Standalone builds, other architectures/configurations, and runtime regression tests were not run.

## Risk

Expected risk to existing WPF code is low based on the inspection and successful build. The execution charset can change the bytes of future non-ASCII ordinary narrow literals; callers must use the matching encoding. The input inspection excludes Windows SDK/toolchain headers and does not establish runtime equivalence across all configurations.

Issues.Title: WPF native build fails with C4819 on Windows code page 936
Issues.Body:
### Description

Building WPF from the .NET VMR fails on Windows x64 with ANSI code page 936 (GBK). MSVC reads UTF-8 files without a BOM using the host code page, and the em dashes in DirectWriteForwarder's TtfDelta comments trigger C4819. The warning is treated as an error.

The affected WPF revision is `e89a851c5792c8777a7115cc7a797fd0c045fdd4`.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Use Windows with ANSI code page 936 and the WPF build prerequisites installed.
2. Build the unmodified WPF revision above from a VMR checkout with dependencies available:

   ```powershell
   .\build.cmd -projects "$PWD\repo-projects\wpf.proj" -configuration Release -rid win-x64 /p:BuildProjectReferences=false -bl
   ```

3. Ensure WPF actually recompiles rather than reusing the VMR repository completion marker. Inspect the WPF log for DirectWriteForwarder errors.

The original `CPP/TrueTypeSubsetter/TtfDelta/ttf_safe_checks.h` and `modsbit.cpp` comments contain em dashes. Direct MSVC comparisons reproduce the failure on source code page 936; selecting UTF-8 or replacing the comment punctuation with ASCII resolves that decoding failure.

### Expected behavior

WPF builds successfully regardless of the host Windows ANSI code page.

### Actual behavior

DirectWriteForwarder reports C4819/C2220. The outer VMR build reports MSB3073 because the WPF command exits with code 1.

With only `/source-charset:utf-8` added, this machine also reports C4566 for `©` in generated C++ assembly copyright attributes. Adding `/execution-charset:utf-8` resolves that second failure and preserves the metadata text.


### Regression?

Reproduces at the revision above. The first affected commit or release has not been established.

### Known Workarounds

ASCII comment replacements resolve the TtfDelta source-decoding failure. Explicit source and execution UTF-8 settings resolve both that failure and the generated copyright-literal failure on this machine.

### Impact

Blocks contributors from building WPF from source on affected Windows configurations. No end-user application regression has been demonstrated.

### Configuration

- Windows x64, ANSI code page 936.
- MSVC 14.51.36231, Visual Studio 2026 toolset.
- WPF Windows x64 Release build through the .NET VMR.
- Validation used process locale `C` for compatibility with the Windows Perl installation. The original MSVC code-page-936 failure was independently verified under that locale.

Issues.Title: Fix temporary WPF assembly identity evaluation
Issues.Body:
Keep path properties and _TargetAssemblyProjectName available during props evaluation, then restore the evaluated AssemblyName and RootNamespace before SDK targets derive output identity.

Fixes #5711 

## Description

WPF markup compilation creates a temporary project when XAML references types from the same assembly. Although the evaluated `AssemblyName` was copied into that project, it was placed before `Sdk.props`. An `AssemblyName` defined in `Directory.Build.props` or a `<Choose>` block could therefore be evaluated again using the temporary project name, causing markup compilation to fail with MC3074.

This change keeps path properties and `_TargetAssemblyProjectName` available before props evaluation, while adding a separate late property group for the evaluated `AssemblyName` and `RootNamespace`. The identity group is inserted immediately before the generated `Sdk.targets` imports, ensuring `TargetName` and related properties are derived from the original project identity.

The insertion logic supports multiple SDKs and projects without an implicit `Sdk` attribute, without using a global property that could flow into referenced projects.

## Customer Impact

Affected WPF projects can build successfully without hard-coding `AssemblyName` or adding temporary-project-specific workarounds. The change applies only during temporary markup compilation and does not alter the final assembly's name or behavior of unaffected projects.

## Regression

Yes

## Risk

Low. The change is limited to property placement in the temporary project used for WPF markup compilation. It preserves the existing early evaluation of path properties and `_TargetAssemblyProjectName`, while restoring the already evaluated `AssemblyName` and `RootNamespace` before SDK targets derive output identity.

Projects whose temporary assembly identity was already correct retain the same evaluated values. The change does not modify the final project’s assembly identity or pass `AssemblyName` as a global property to referenced projects.

Issues.Body:
Branch [release/8.0](https://github.com/dotnet/wpf/commits/release/8.0/) in `dotnet/wpf` repo can't be mirrored from GitHub to Azure [internal/release/8.0](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-wpf?version=GBinternal%2Frelease%2F8.0&_a=history) via internal merge. 

There are conflicting commits in the target branch.
The branch is configured to be mirrored via automated merge. 
The situation is rare but normal. The target branch is expected to receive manual commits in the Azure DevOps clone, which could cause conflict.

Conflicts need to be **resolved to unblock the code flow**.

- you can resolve the issue by resolving the conflict in the **target branch only**. 
    - Please make sure that the changes sensitive from security perspective are not published ahead of time to GitHub!
- reverting the extra commits in the Azdo target branch.
- checking the logs of the mirroring process in the [mirroring pipeline](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_build?definitionId=1387).
- you can disable the mirroring of the branch in the [configuration file](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-mirroring?path=/dnceng-subscriptions.jsonc).
- you can ask @dotnet/dnceng for help or read the [documentation](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-mirroring?path=/README.md).

Please close this issue once the conflict is resolved.

Issues.Title: Fix providing EnhancedMetafile to other applications through the clip…
Issues.Body:
Fixes #11986

Depends on dotnet/winforms#15218. 

This PR has to merge before that change flows into WPF, or WPF won't build.

## Description

On .NET 10, the shared OLE code in System.Private.Windows.Core rejects every `TYMED_ENHMF` request with `DV_E_TYMED`, so WPF can't provide `CF_ENHMETAFILE` to other applications even though the format is still advertised.

- Add `WpfOleServices.AllowedTymeds`, which also allows `TYMED_ENHMF`. It implements the new `IOleServices.AllowedTymeds` from dotnet/winforms#TBD.
- Fix the `TYMED_ENHMF` branch of `WpfOleServices.GetDataHere`, which was unreachable until now. For a `MemoryStream` it never assigned the handle to the medium, so it returned `S_OK` with a null handle. It now sets `tymed` and `hEnhMetaFile`, and returns `E_FAIL` when there is no handle, as .NET 9 did.
- Add a clipboard test that reads the EMF back with `GetClipboardData`, the way another application would. It's skipped until the winforms change flows in.

I'd like to request a backport to `release/10.0` after this merges.

## Customer Impact

EMF that WPF apps put on the clipboard can't be pasted into other applications, for example Word's Paste Special → Picture (Enhanced Metafile). It fails silently, and there's no workaround.

## Regression

Yes. It works on .NET 9 and is broken on .NET 10.

## Testing

- `build.cmd -pack` succeeds, both against the current `Microsoft.Private.Winforms` package and against a local build of dotnet/winforms#15218.
- Built against dotnet/winforms#15218, the new test passes for `copy: true` and `copy: false`.
- End-to-end on .NET 11 RC 1, a test app can now read the EMF through `GetClipboardData(CF_ENHMETAFILE)` and OLE `GetData`, for delayed and flushed data. The unpatched runtime fails all three checks.

## Risk

Low. It only affects `TYMED_ENHMF` requests for `EnhancedMetafile` data, which always fail today, and restores the .NET 9 behavior.

Issues.Title: Fix culture invariance of ArcSegment's RotationAngle during XPS serialization
Issues.Body:
Fixes #11983 

## Description

Fixes the serialization of `ArcSegment.RotationAngle` property to be culture invariant during XPS serialization. This is in line with how all other floating number values in XPS always have been serialized to avoid parsing ambiguity in the resulting markup.

## Customer Impact

Customers will be able to print on threads regardless of their current culture setting, as intended.

## Regression

Nope, this is already present in NETFX.

## Testing

I didn't include tests this time since it requires a new project (we don't have one public for ReachFramework in this repo nor they've been opensourced as part of wpf-test, and this change doesn't justify doing it for me).

## Risk

Virtually none, it would have been previously rejected altogether, if fractional.

Issues.Title: XPS serialization writes ArcSegment.RotationAngle with the current culture (VisualSerializer.cs), decimal comma yields invalid page markup
Issues.Body:
### Description

When a `FixedDocument` containing an elliptical arc with a fractional rotation angle is serialized to XPS (`XpsDocumentWriter.Write`, and the XPS path used by `PrintDialog.PrintDocument`) on a thread whose culture uses a decimal comma, the rotation angle is written with the comma, e.g. `-168,65`.

In the XPS path mini-language the comma is a separator, so the arc segment `A rx,ry angle isLargeArc sweep x,y`gets the wrong number of parameters and the page markup is invalid.

All other numbers of the same path (radii, points) are written culture-invariantly; only the rotation angle is affected.

Observed output (same path, only the thread culture differs):

    de-DE: M0,0L39,16A207.14,193.14 -168,65 0 0 124,33L172,33
    en-US: M0,0L39,16A207.14,193.14 -168.65 0 0 124,33L172,33

In our application this surfaces when printing to "Microsoft Print to PDF" with a de-DE / pl-PL culture:`IXpsOMObjectFactory.CreatePageFromStream` fails with `COMException 0x8052000C` (`XPS_E_INVALID_MARKUP`), WPF aborts the job without throwing to the caller, and the output file stays at 0 bytes. The same content prints correctly when the thread culture is `InvariantCulture`.

## Root cause

`src/Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf/src/ReachFramework/Serialization/VisualSerializer.cs`, in the `ArcSegment` branch of the path data builder (line 1310 on `main` at the time of writing):

    rslt.Append('A');
    AppendPoint(rslt, new Point(s.Width * map.M11, s.Height * map.M22), Matrix.Identity);
    rslt.Append(' ');
    rslt.Append(a.RotationAngle);      // StringBuilder.Append(double) uses CultureInfo.CurrentCulture
    rslt.Append(' ');

The surrounding code consistently uses `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` (`AppendPoint`, the matrix and viewbox formatting, `WriteAttr`). This is the only `StringBuilder.Append` of a floating-point value in that file that does not.

## Suggested fix

    rslt.Append(a.RotationAngle.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture));

(Other serializers in the same file additionally go through `CheckFloat`; it may be worth applying it here as well.)

### Reproduction Steps

Attached is a minimal console project (`ArcCultureRepro`, .NET 10, WPF).
[ArcCultureRepro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32850446/ArcCultureRepro.zip)

1. `dotnet run -c Release -- de-DE`
2. The program serializes a one-page `FixedDocument` with a single `Path`(`M 0,0 L 39,16 A 207.139,193.142 -168.65 0 0 124,33 L 172,33`) to an .xps file and prints the arc as it appears in the generated page markup.
3. Compare with `dotnet run -c Release -- en-US`.

Optional: add `--print` to send the same document through `PrintDialog.PrintDocument` to "Microsoft Print to PDF".

### Expected behavior

The rotation angle is written culture-invariantly (`-168.65`) regardless of the thread culture.

### Actual behavior

The rotation angle is written with the thread culture (`-168,65`), which produces invalid XPS markup.

### Regression?

_No response_

### Known Workarounds

Set `CultureInfo.CurrentCulture = CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` for the duration of the print/serialization call and restore it afterwards.



### Impact

When printing to "Microsoft Print to PDF" with a de-DE / pl-PL culture, WPF aborts the job without throwing to the caller, and the output file stays at 0 bytes.

### Configuration

* .NET 10.0.12 (WindowsDesktop runtime)
* Windows 11
* Thread culture de-DE (customer: pl-PL)

### Other information

_No response_

### Expected behavior

A single click on last value in the viewport should directly toggle the checkbox state without causing any scrolling.

### Actual behavior

Clicking the CheckBox of the last visible item in the viewport does not toggle the CheckBox state. Instead, the ScrollViewer automatically scrolls and brings additional items into view.

Issues.Title: Add WindowChrome DWM caption/backdrop support
Issues.Body:
Introduce modern DWM-driven window chrome: add CaptionTextColorHelper and WindowCaptionAdorner; extend WindowChrome with new enums/properties (FrameMode, CaptionTheme, BackdropType, CornerPreference, caption/border/text colors) and read-only attached properties for per-window state. Rewrite WindowChromeWorker to manage extended-client-area, DWM attributes, backdrop, DPI-aware frame insets, caption buttons and adorner. Expand NativeMethods and Utilities for new DWM/monitor/AppBar APIs. Remove legacy WindowBackdropManager and WindowBackdropType. Integrate with ThemeManager and update Ribbon templates to use WindowChrome extended mode. Add comprehensive unit tests for caption color, frame insets and WindowChrome behavior. Update project includes and internals visibility for tests.

Fixes #11973 11973

## Description

Introduces modern DWM-driven window chrome integration for WindowChrome:
- New CaptionTextColorHelper and WindowCaptionAdorner
- New WindowChrome properties/enums: FrameMode, CaptionTheme, BackdropType, CornerPreference, caption/border/text colors, plus read-only attached properties for per-window state
- WindowChromeWorker rewritten to manage extended client area, DWM attributes, backdrop, DPI-aware frame insets, caption buttons and the adorner
- Expanded NativeMethods/Utilities for the new DWM/monitor/AppBar APIs
- Removed legacy WindowBackdropManager/WindowBackdropType
- Ribbon templates and ThemeManager updated to use the new extended chrome mode
- Added unit tests for caption color, frame insets and WindowChrome behavior

## Customer Impact

Enables apps to opt into native Mica/Acrylic backdrops, rounded corner preference, and DWM-driven caption/border theming without custom chrome hacks.

## Regression

No known regressions have been observed when the new opt-in properties are not used. Because this change substantially updates `WindowChromeWorker`, additional review and testing are still needed for existing custom-chrome scenarios.

## Testing

Added unit tests for the managed property and frame-inset behavior. Native DWM behavior, rendering, DPI transitions, and caption-button interaction were manually verified on Windows 11 (including dpi and high contrast theme).

## Risk

Touches `WindowChromeWorker` internals broadly. The changes are covered by unit tests where practical and are gated behind new opt-in properties. Some behavior, including native DWM integration, rendering, DPI transitions, and caption-button interaction, requires manual validation on supported Windows configurations.

Issues.Title: [API Proposal]: WindowChrome extensions for system frame integration, DWM caption/border colors, corner preference, backdrop and extended client area
Issues.Body:
### Background and motivation `System.Windows.Shell.WindowChrome` currently only supports **fully custom chrome**: WPF paints the whole non-client area itself and the system frame is not involved beyond hit-testing/resizing. This proposal extends `WindowChrome` with two more first-class modes — keeping the **system frame** while only customizing its DWM appearance (colors, corners, theme, backdrop), and an **extended client area** mode where the system caption buttons stay live while WPF content flows under/around them (similar to WinUI 3's `ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar`). It also exposes the modern DWM window attributes (caption/text/border color, corner preference, dark caption, Mica/Acrylic/Tabbed backdrop) as bindable properties, and adds read-only attached properties that let arbitrary content correctly avoid or align with the system-drawn caption buttons. This closes long-standing gaps where custom-titlebar WPF apps had to either fully reimplement the caption buttons (losing snap-layout flyouts, accessibility, and touch/keyboard behavior) or fall back to raw P/Invoke to get Windows 11 Mica/Acrylic, dark titlebars, or rounded corners. It also formalizes (as public, documented API) backdrop/immersive-dark-mode behavior that today exists only as private support for the Fluent theme (`WindowBackdropManager`, `Window.SetImmersiveDarkMode`, both internal). Property reference Property | Type | Values / meaning | Default -- | -- | -- | -- `FrameMode` | `WindowChromeFrameMode` | `Custom` — WPF fully owns the non-client area; `ExtendedClientArea` — system frame/buttons stay active, client area extends under the caption; `SystemFrame` — system frame untouched, only caption appearance/backdrop are managed. | `Custom` `ShowSystemIcon` | `bool?` | `true` shows the system icon; `false` hides it; `null` defers to `FrameMode`: shown in `Custom`/`SystemFrame`, hidden in `ExtendedClientArea`. | `null` `ShowTitle` | `bool?` | `true` shows the title; `false` hides it; `null` defers to `FrameMode`: shown in `Custom`/`SystemFrame`, hidden in `ExtendedClientArea`. | `null` `CaptionColor` | `Color?` | Any `Color`; alpha ignored **unless** a backdrop is active, in which case a fully transparent color asks DWM not to paint the caption at all so the backdrop shows through even when the system is set to color titlebars (`DWMWA_COLOR_NONE`). `null` restores the system-chosen caption color. Requires Windows 11. | `null` `CaptionTextColor` | `Color?` | Any `Color`; alpha channel ignored. `null` restores the system-chosen text color. Requires Windows 11. | `null` `BorderColor` | `Color?` | Any `Color`; `null` restores the default border; a color with alpha `0` removes the border. Requires Windows 11. | `null` `CornerPreference` | `WindowCornerPreference` | `Default` — system choice; `DoNotRound`; `Round`; `RoundSmall` — smaller radius. Requires Windows 11. | `Default` `CaptionTheme` | `WindowCaptionTheme` | `Auto` — follows Fluent/framework theme, otherwise system; `Light`; `Dark`. Requires Windows 10 1809+. | `Auto` `BackdropType` | `WindowBackdropKind` | `Auto` — Mica for Fluent windows, none otherwise; `None`; `Mica`; `Acrylic`; `Tabbed` — Mica Alt. Requires Windows 11 22H2+. | `Auto` `CaptionButtonsBounds` | `Rect`, read-only attached | Rect in DIPs, relative to client origin, occupied by the system caption buttons; `default(Rect)` if the system isn't drawing them over the client area. | `default(Rect)` `CaptionButtonsClip` | `Geometry`, read-only attached | Frozen geometry covering the whole client area except `CaptionButtonsBounds`, meant to be bound to an element's `Clip` so it never paints over the caption buttons; expressed in client-origin coordinates (not suitable for nested/offset elements). `null` when the system isn't drawing the buttons over the client area. | `null` `TitleBarBounds` | `Rect`, read-only attached | Rect in DIPs for app content within the caption band, excluding `CaptionButtonsBounds`; `default(Rect)` when not applicable. | `default(Rect)` `CaptionForeground` | `Brush`, read-only attached | Brush computed by system/framework for caption text, accounting for active state, accent color, theme, and `CaptionColor`/`CaptionTextColor`. | `SystemColors.ActiveCaptionTextBrush` `IsCaptionCustomizationSupported` | `bool`, static read-only | `true` on Windows 11+; otherwise `false`. | OS-dependent `IsBackdropSupported` | `bool`, static read-only | `true` on Windows 11 22H2+; otherwise `false`. | OS-dependent | `CaptionButtonRole` | `CaptionButtonRole`, attached | `None` — ordinary element; `Minimize`/`Maximize`/`Close` — marks the element as standing in for that system caption button, for a chrome that draws the caption itself (`Custom` mode without system-drawn buttons; ignored while the system draws its own). The system then treats the element as its own button: it shows the window layout flyout when the pointer rests on `Maximize`, and a click invokes the element (its command or click handler) or, when the element cannot be invoked, performs the window command of the role. | `None` | | `IsCaptionButtonHovered` | `bool`, read-only attached | Set on an element with a `CaptionButtonRole`: whether the pointer is over it. Since the system owns the pointer over such an element, regular mouse-over state is never received, so this replaces it. | `false` | | `IsCaptionButtonPressed` | `bool`, read-only attached | Set on an element with a `CaptionButtonRole`: whether the primary mouse button is held down over it. Replaces the regular pressed state, which the element does not receive for the same reason. | `false` |

Issues.Title: Regression in Clipboard/DataObject text conversion
Issues.Body:
### Description

The text in clipboard/data object seems to be no longer auto-converted between Text and UnicodeText format.

### Reproduction Steps

```C#
DataObject d = new DataObject();
d.SetText("ahoj", TextDataFormat.Text);

Clipboard.SetDataObject(d);

var present = Clipboard.GetDataObject().GetDataPresent("UnicodeText");
var hasText = Clipboard.ContainsText();
var hasUnicode = Clipboard.ContainsText(TextDataFormat.UnicodeText);
```

### Expected behavior

returns true for all calls, which is the case in .NET up to 9.0

### Actual behavior

returns false for all calls

### Regression?

yes, works in .NET 9 and before 

### Known Workarounds

_No response_

### Impact

Applications cannot access text in clipboard/drag data.

### Configuration

.NET 10.0.11
Windows 11 (x64 29667)
